column1: # KASOTI model-fetch manifest — REAL manifest (spike 01, docs/spikes/01-face-model.md)
# Consumed by:  ./scripts/fetch_models.sh scripts/models_manifest.tsv
# Verified by:  ./scripts/verify_bundle.sh   (invariant I12 / AT-12)
# FORMAT (whitespace separated, one entry per line):
#     <64 lowercase hex sha256>  <https url>  <destination path, repo-relative>
# Lines beginning with '#' and blank lines are ignored. The URL MUST be https.
# Model binaries are NOT committed (.gitignore excludes *.tflite and eval/models/).
# Each entry is downloaded to a temp file, hashed, and only then moved into place; a
# file that fails verification is DELETED, never installed. Nothing is ever fetched at
# runtime — the apps load the same bytes from bundled assets only.
# PROVENANCE OF THE HASHES BELOW (AGENTS.md §8: never invent a hash)
# Google publishes NO .sha256 sidecar for the BlazeFace model (the sidecar URL returns
# HTTP 404). Every digest here was MEASURED by us on 2026-09-30 from the bytes served
# at the URL on that line, using:
#     ./scripts/fetch_models.sh scripts/models_manifest.tsv --record
# which downloads, hashes and prints, without installing. A pin produced that way is a
# pin of an artefact we actually fetched. A pin typed from memory is not, and the script
# cannot tell the difference — only the operator can.
# The URLs use the VERSIONED path (`/float16/1/`), never the `/latest/` alias that
# Google's documentation links to. Both were byte-identical when checked, but `latest`
# can be repointed under us and a pin against a moving alias is not a pin (RT-E8).
# --- face DETECTOR: obtained, licence-verified, adopted ---------------------------
# BlazeFace short-range, float16. Model card:
#   https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-assets/MediaPipe%20BlazeFace%20Model%20Card%20(Short%20Range).pdf
# Licence: Apache-2.0, stated on that card. Redistribution in a repo or a shipped binary
# is permitted; no rider, no click-through, no per-user registration.
# Training data: "consented images of people using a mobile AR application".
# Authors: Valentin Bazarevsky et al. (Google), 2019; card dated 2021-06-09.
# Paper: arXiv:2006.10204.
# Stated-scope caveat, carried in docs/spikes/01-face-model.md §6.1 and docs/STATUS.md:
# the model card lists "any form of surveillance or identity recognition" as explicitly
# out of scope. Apache-2.0 permits our use; the authors documented the opposite boundary.
# This is a lead decision, not an engineering one.
# 229,746 bytes. Android + desktop, same file, TFLite (DESIGN D1).

b4578f35940bf5a1a655214a1cce5cab13eba73c1297cd78e1a04c2380b0152f  https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/face_detector/blaze_face_short_range/float16/1/blaze_face_short_range.tflite  eval/models/blazeface_short.tflite
# There is deliberately NO line here. Seven candidates were evaluated and rejected on
# licence grounds, and no weights were fabricated, approximated or synthesised to fill
# the slot. Full evidence per candidate: docs/spikes/01-face-model.md §2.1.
#   A  sirius-ai/MobileFaceNet_TF    Apache-2.0 code, no TFLite file, trained on
#                                    MS1M/VGGFace2 (non-commercial data)
#   B  DXG-INF/GhostFaceNet          upstream repository is gone (HTTP 404)
#   B' HamadYA/GhostFaceNets         MIT code, .h5 not TFLite, 512-d not 128-d, MS1MV2/3
#   C  deepghs/edgeface              upstream repository is gone (HTTP 404)
#   D  MediaPipe face embedder       never published: the mediapipe-models bucket has
#                                    no face_embedder/ prefix at all
#   E  InsightFace buffalo_l         "non-commercial research purposes only"; licensing
#                                    now requires an email (2025-11-24)
#   F  OpenCV Zoo SFace              ONNX not TFLite, ~37 MB, MS1MV2 training data
# Consequence: the face layer can locate a face but cannot compare one, so a GREEN
# 1:1 verdict stays unreachable. `face = null` -> face layer UNAVAILABLE -> GREEN
# blocked (FUSION.md §7). That is the correct fail-closed behaviour, not a defect.
# Filling this slot is a LICENSING decision for the lead, not a fetching task for an
# engineer. See docs/spikes/01-face-model.md §8.
